title: What If an Avalanche Buried You? The Clock Is Brutal

scenes.text: What if an avalanche buried you? Your odds come down to one number: minutes.
In a big Swiss study of completely buried people, about 91 percent survived if they were dug out within 18 minutes.
Then the curve collapses. By 35 minutes, survival drops to about 34 percent.
Up to that point, the main killer is suffocation. The snow packs tight around the chest and the air runs out.
After 35 minutes survival stays roughly flat until about 90 minutes, when cold becomes the threat.
So the first 18 minutes belong to whoever is standing next to you. Help from outside usually arrives too late.
